result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [SDTMVariableSpec]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The specification of one variable in an SDTM domain template. twitter-card: title: >- [SDTMVariableSpec]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The specification of one variable in an SDTM domain template. title: >- [SDTMVariableSpec]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The specification of one variable in an SDTM domain template. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The specification of one variable in an SDTM domain template. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_sdtm_templates.py#L16-L83){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature SDTMVariableSpec( name, label, dtype, role, required=False, max_length=None, controlled_term=None, core="Perm", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} An [`SDTMDomainTemplate`](`pointblank.SDTMDomainTemplate`) holds an `SDTMVariableSpec` for each variable of its domain, in its `variables` list. The specification gives what the SDTM Implementation Guide says about the variable: its label, its type, its role in the domain, its core designation, and the controlled terminology for its values. [`validate_sdtm()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtm`) uses `required`, `dtype`, `max_length` and `role` to decide which checks to make. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The variable name, such as `"STUDYID"` or `"AESTDTC"`. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The variable label, such as `"Study Identifier"`. [dtype]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The SDTM data type: `"Char"` for character variables or `"Num"` for numeric ones. [role]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The variable's SDTM role. The templates use `"Identifier"` (variables that identify the study, subject, domain or record), `"Topic"` (the focus of the observation, such as `AETERM`), `"Qualifier"` (variables that describe the observation) and `"Timing"` (dates, times and study days). [required]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the variable is required: it must be in the dataset and can't be null. In the templates, this is `True` exactly when `core` is `"Req"`. The default is `False`. [max_length]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The maximum length of the values of a character variable. The default is `None` (no maximum, as for numeric variables). [controlled_term]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The name of the controlled terminology codelist for the variable's values, such as `"SEX"` or `"NY"`. The default is `None`. [core]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["Perm"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The core designation: `"Req"` (required), `"Exp"` (expected: in the dataset, but values may be null) or `"Perm"` (permissible: included when there is data for it). The default is `"Perm"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Specifications are usually taken from a template. Here is the one for `AESER` in the Adverse Events (AE) template: ::: {#a73425bf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb aeser = pb.get_sdtm_domain("AE").get_variable("AESER") aeser ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` SDTMVariableSpec(name='AESER', label='Serious Event', dtype='Char', role='Qualifier', required=False, max_length=2, controlled_term='NY', core='Exp') ``` ::: ::: `AESER` (whether the adverse event was serious) is an expected character variable of at most two characters, with values from the `NY` (No Yes Response) codelist. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~SDTMDomainTemplate`) : The template that holds the specifications of a domain's variables. [](`~ADaMVariableSpec`) : The equivalent for ADaM dataset templates.
